title: Dissipation-selected photon-phonon pair and photon-bundle emission in a tripartite Mollow system
authors: Jiayuan Zhang, Geng Zhao, Jing Tang, Yuangang Deng
abstract: Dissipation is generally regarded as detrimental to nonclassical-state generation, yet whether it can determine which quantum resource is emitted from an open hybrid quantum system remains largely unexplored. Here, we show that the symmetry of bosonic dissipation channels can select and switch quantum-emission pathways in a tripartite Mollow system, where a strongly driven two-level emitter simultaneously couples to cavity photons and motional phonons. In the Mollow regime, higher-order tripartite interactions generate resonant photon-phonon pair excitations, whose emitted quantum states are subsequently selected by dissipation. Under symmetric dissipation, the system produces strongly correlated photon-phonon pairs, enabling both single-pair emission and correlated multipair bundles with pronounced nonclassical correlations. Breaking the dissipation symmetry progressively suppresses the hybrid correlations and dynamically decouples the photonic and phononic degrees of freedom. In the strongly asymmetric regime, long-lived phonons accumulate in highly excited Fock states, while rapidly leaking cavity photons are converted into high-purity single-photon and two-photon bundles. The crossover between these distinct emission regimes is characterized through time-resolved correlation functions, Fock-state distributions, and Wigner quasiprobability distributions. Our results establish dissipation symmetry as a resource for steering quantum emission between hybrid and purely photonic nonclassical states, providing a route toward programmable hybrid quantum emitters and dissipative quantum-state engineering.
summary: This paper demonstrates that the symmetry of dissipation in a tripartite Mollow system can actively control the quantum emission pathway. By tuning the dissipation symmetry, the system can be forced to emit either highly correlated photon-phonon pairs or distinct photon bundles. This establishes dissipation symmetry as a powerful resource for programmable hybrid quantum emitters.
main_problem: The study investigates whether dissipation can actively determine or select the type of quantum resource (e.g., correlated pairs vs. photon bundles) emitted from an open hybrid quantum system, rather than simply causing decoherence.
main_result: Dissipation symmetry acts as a controllable resource, allowing the system to steer quantum emission between correlated photon-phonon pairs (under symmetric dissipation) and purely photonic nonclassical states (under asymmetric dissipation).
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad master equation to model the open system dynamics and characterizes emission using time-resolved correlation functions, Fock-state distributions, and Wigner quasiprobability distributions.
model_or_system: The system is a tripartite Mollow setup involving a strongly driven two-level emitter coupled simultaneously to cavity photons and motional phonons. The dynamics are governed by an effective Hamiltonian derived in the Mollow regime.
key_observables: Time-delayed second-order correlation functions ($g^{(2)}$), Fock-state distributions, and Wigner quasiprobability distributions.
important_parameters: The dissipation ratio ($\kappa_a/\kappa_b$) is the key control parameter, determining the emission regime (symmetric vs. asymmetric dissipation).
main_assumptions: The system dynamics are modeled using effective Hamiltonians derived under the rotating-wave approximation, and the selection mechanism is attributed to the symmetry of the bosonic dissipation channels.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the switching between pair and bundle emission by tuning the dissipation ratio ($\kappa_a/\kappa_b$), and another figure shows the dressed-state structure in the Mollow regime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the tripartite Mollow model, deriving effective Hamiltonians for $N$-pair processes, and then analyzing the resulting emission regimes—symmetric (pair emission) versus asymmetric (bundle emission)—by controlling the dissipation symmetry.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the frontier of open quantum systems, demonstrating that engineered dissipation can be a constructive tool for quantum state engineering, moving beyond its traditional role as a source of loss.
